flagged.evidence: The cited `lem-cm-piecewise-c1-jump-derivative` states that “p is continuous on I\{t_*}” and permits an arbitrary value at `t_*`. Here [L1] instead says `p:I→R` is continuous on all of `I`, and proof step 2.1 asserts each `p_{i,k}` is continuous. The model fixes `p_i(t_*)=0` but allows nonzero one-sided momentum limits, so that continuity need not hold. The lemma covers the intended punctured-domain case, but its hypotheses are misstated and the application as written is not licensed.

Step 2.1 defines `c=√(2E/μ)`. The energy identity in [L1] gives, at every finite `ρ`, `|ρ'|²=c²−2κ/(μρ)−J²/(μρ²)<c²` because `κ,J>0`. Thus step 4.1's assertion `|ρ'|≥c` is false. The asserted lower bound `ρ(t)≥c|t|` up to an additive constant is also not established; the limit `|ρ'|→c` only supplies an eventual lower bound using a fixed `c₀<c`.

The clause says “Let `r:J₀→R³` be the relative coordinate of a motion” and then treats `t∈J₀` as time, but the referenced central-model definition uses `J₀⊂(0,∞)` for the radial domain of the potential and names the time window `I₀`. This item never declares `J₀` as a time interval, so its trajectory domain is undeclared and conflated with the potential domain.

The example assumes a C¹ velocity field with `u=4 x̂` on an inlet whose normal is `−x̂`, while `u·ν=0` on the impermeable remainder. The control-volume theorem requires `u` to be C¹ on an open neighborhood of the closed control region, and a bounded C¹ boundary has a continuous outward normal; hence `u·ν` is continuous on the boundary. Its trace is `−4 m s⁻¹` on the inlet and `0` on the remainder, which cannot meet continuously at their partition interfaces. The stated positive-area inlet with constant normal cannot be an entire closed boundary component, so such an interface must occur. Thus the declared field premises cannot be realized as stated.
